It appears during the reign of enlightened rulers.

claims.statement: The National Palace Museum holds a Luduan-shaped bronze incense burner with gold and silver inlay.
claims.statement_id: Museum Istana Nasional menyimpan pedupaan perunggu berbentuk Luduan dengan tatahan emas dan perak.
claims.quote: Bronze incense burner in the shape of luduan with gold and silver inlay

claims.statement: A legend says a luduan once appeared to Genghis Khan and persuaded him to abandon his efforts to conquer India.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah legenda menyebut luduan pernah menampakkan diri kepada Genghis Khan dan meyakinkannya untuk membatalkan upayanya menaklukkan India.
claims.quote: A legend says a luduan once appeared to Genghis Khan and convinced him to abandon his efforts to conquer India.

claims.statement: The Emperor's throne in the Hall of Supreme Harmony has two incense burners shaped like the luduan as an auspicious symbol.
claims.statement_id: Singgasana Kaisar di Aula Keharmonisan Tertinggi memiliki dua pedupaan berbentuk luduan sebagai lambang keberuntungan.
claims.quote: The throne of the Emperor in the Hall of Supreme Harmony has two incense burners shaped like the luduan as an auspicious symbol.

claims.statement: A Chinese history text records a one-horned beast shaped like a deer with a horse's tail and a green color that spoke like a human and told the attendants: "Your lord should return early."
claims.statement_id: Sebuah teks sejarah Tiongkok mencatat makhluk bertanduk satu berbentuk seperti rusa dengan ekor kuda dan berwarna hijau yang berbicara seperti manusia dan berkata kepada para pengawal: "Tuanmu sebaiknya cepat kembali."
claims.quote: 有一角獸，形如鹿而馬尾，其色綠，作人言，謂侍衞者曰：「汝主宜早還。」

claims.statement: When the emperor asked Chucai (楚材), he answered that it was an auspicious beast named 角端 (jiaoduan), able to speak the languages of the four directions, who loves life and hates killing, and that it was a sign sent from heaven to the emperor.
claims.statement_id: Ketika sang kaisar bertanya kepada Chucai (楚材), ia menjawab bahwa makhluk itu adalah binatang pertanda baik bernama 角端 (jiaoduan) yang mampu berbicara dalam bahasa empat penjuru, menyukai kehidupan dan membenci pembunuhan, dan merupakan tanda dari langit bagi sang kaisar.
claims.quote: 帝以問楚材，對曰：「此瑞獸也，其名角端，能言四方語，好生惡殺，此天降符以告陛下。

claims.statement: Chucai urges the emperor to follow heaven's will so as to preserve the people's lives, and the emperor withdrew his army that very day.
claims.statement_id: Chucai mendesak sang kaisar menaati kehendak langit demi menyelamatkan nyawa rakyat, dan sang kaisar menarik pasukannya pada hari itu juga.
claims.quote: 陛下天之元子，天下之人皆陛下之子，願承天心，以全民命。」帝即日班師。

claims.statement: Mo-sin-a is a Taiwanese folkloric creature portrayed as short and hairy with a human-like form.
claims.statement_id: Mo-sin-a adalah makhluk dalam cerita rakyat Taiwan berbentuk manusia pendek berbulu.
claims.quote: The Mo-sin-a (Chinese: 魔神仔; Pe̍h-ōe-jī: Mô͘-sîn-á) is a monstrous creature in Taiwanese folklore. They are typically depicted as human-like beings and their bodies are short and furry.

claims.statement: Accounts place it in mountain forests and link it with luring people into remote places.
claims.statement_id: Kisah menempatkannya di hutan pegunungan dan mengaitkannya dengan pengalihan orang ke tempat terpencil.
claims.quote: The mo-sin-a are considered a type of demon who lives in mountain forests. They are said to lure people away to remote spots like mountain forests or caves. Japanese-era newspapers mention it several times, and the demon was featured in the horror movie series, The Tag-Along.

claims.statement: Japanese-period newspapers mention this creature several times.
claims.statement_id: Surat kabar masa Jepang menyebut makhluk ini beberapa kali.
claims.quote: The mo-sin-a are considered a type of demon who lives in mountain forests. They are said to lure people away to remote spots like mountain forests or caves. Japanese-era newspapers mention it several times, and the demon was featured in the horror movie series, The Tag-Along.

claims.statement: The 魔神仔 (mo-sin-a) is described as a mountain or water spirit-monster, small in size, able to transform (幻化) and play tricks on people; the "Little Girl in Red" (紅衣小女孩) and the "玉山黃色小飛俠" are said to be kinds of 魔神仔.
claims.statement_id: 魔神仔 (Mo-sin-a) digambarkan sebagai siluman gunung dan air yang bertubuh kecil, dapat berubah rupa (幻化), dan suka mengusili orang; "Gadis Kecil Berbaju Merah" (紅衣小女孩) dan "玉山黃色小飛俠" disebut sebagai jenis-jenis 魔神仔.
claims.quote: 「魔神仔」是山精水怪，矮矮小小的，會幻化、會作弄人，臺灣民間傳說中最知名的「紅衣小女孩」、登山客絕對不想遇到的「玉山黃色小飛俠」，都是魔神仔的一種。

claims.statement: In the stories, people taken away by the 魔神仔 are found in trees or caves, and the 魔神仔 ask people for clothes; the researcher links the first to early humans' jungle life and the second to the advance of civilization and a sense of shame.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah-kisahnya, orang yang dibawa pergi 魔神仔 ditemukan di pohon atau gua, dan 魔神仔 meminta pakaian dari orang; peneliti mengaitkan yang pertama dengan pengalaman hidup di hutan manusia awal dan yang kedua dengan kemajuan peradaban serta rasa malu.
claims.quote: 例如，在樹上或是洞穴發現被魔神仔帶走的人，這可以連結到早期人類的叢林生活經驗；而魔神仔跟人要衣服穿，則是與人類文明的進展相關，是一種羞恥心的展現。

claims.statement: When someone is "spirited away" (神隱) in the mountains, people call out the name of the person taken by the 魔神仔; the researcher likens this naming to humans passing from nameless to named.
claims.statement_id: Bila seseorang "disembunyikan dewa" (神隱) di pegunungan, orang berteriak memanggil nama orang yang dibawa 魔神仔; cara memanggil nama ini disamakan peneliti dengan manusia yang beralih dari tanpa nama menjadi bernama.
claims.quote: 當有人在山區被神隱，要大聲呼喊被魔神仔帶走的人的名字，這種呼喚名字的方式，如同人類從無名到有名

claims.statement: The 魔神仔 plays tricks on people in the wild, whereas ghost stories arise after someone has died in a place, so the two are distinguished.
claims.statement_id: 魔神仔 mengusili orang di alam liar, sedangkan cerita hantu muncul setelah seseorang meninggal di suatu tempat, sehingga keduanya dibedakan.
claims.quote: 魔神仔是在野外捉弄人，而鬼是一個地方有人死掉以後，產生鬼故事。

claims.statement: The screenwriter of the Taiwanese horror film 《紅衣小女孩》, 簡士耕, said he was inspired to write it after taking 林美容's class and reading 《魔神仔的人類學想像》.
claims.statement_id: Penulis skenario film horor Taiwan 《紅衣小女孩》, 簡士耕, pernah menyatakan bahwa ia terinspirasi menulisnya setelah mengikuti kelas 林美容 dan membaca 《魔神仔的人類學想像》.
claims.quote: 臺灣恐怖電影《紅衣小女孩》的編劇簡士耕曾表示，他是上了林美容的課、讀了《魔神仔的人類學想像》，才啟發他創作《紅衣小女孩》。

claims.statement: 林美容 holds that Taiwanese society should treat 魔神仔 legends as cultural heritage and use these spirits as local material to help people know Taiwan's culture.
claims.statement_id: 林美容 berpendapat bahwa masyarakat Taiwan semestinya memperlakukan kisah-kisah 魔神仔 sebagai warisan budaya dan memakainya sebagai bahan lokal agar orang mengenal budaya Taiwan.
claims.quote: 林美容認為臺灣社會應該把魔神仔的傳說故事當作一種文化資產，可以把這些鬼怪當成鄉土素材來利用，讓大家認識臺灣的文化。

claims.statement: Panhu is a figure in Han and Yao mythology and in several groups' origin stories.
claims.statement_id: Panhu adalah tokoh mitologi Han dan Yao serta kisah asal-usul sejumlah kelompok.
claims.quote: Panhu (hanzi: 盤瓠; pinyin Pánhù; IPA: /pʰan³⁵-xu⁵¹/) is an important figure in Han and Yao mythologies. The Panhu mythological complex includes myths in Chinese and also other languages.

claims.statement: The central tale describes a dragon-dog becoming a man and marrying a princess.
claims.statement_id: Kisah dasarnya menceritakan anjing naga yang menjadi manusia dan menikahi putri.
claims.quote: The basic Panhu myth is about a dragon-dog who transformed into a man and married a princess. In the myth, there was an old woman in an ancient Chinese king's palace who had ear pain for many years. A royal physician plucked out a small, golden worm from her ear, and placed it inside of a gourd covered with a plate.

claims.statement: One version begins with a golden worm removed from a palace woman's ear.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah versi bermula dari cacing emas yang dikeluarkan dari telinga perempuan di istana.
claims.quote: The basic Panhu myth is about a dragon-dog who transformed into a man and married a princess. In the myth, there was an old woman in an ancient Chinese king's palace who had ear pain for many years. A royal physician plucked out a small, golden worm from her ear, and placed it inside of a gourd covered with a plate.

claims.statement: In some variants, the human transformation remains incomplete and the dog head persists.
claims.statement_id: Dalam varian tertentu, perubahan menjadi manusia tidak selesai dan kepala anjing tetap ada.
claims.quote: There are also variant versions. In some variants, the dragon-dog became transformed into a human, except for his head. This is sometimes attributed to the princess worrying that he was starving inside the golden vessel he was placed inside of for seven days and seven nights to transform into a human, which resulted in the process being incomplete.

claims.statement: Panhu accounts have more historicized and more mythological versions.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Panhu memiliki versi yang lebih historis dan versi yang lebih mitologis.
claims.quote: In the study of historical Chinese culture, many of the stories that have been told regarding characters and events which have been written or told of the distant past have a double tradition: one which presents a more historicized version and one which presents a more mythological version. This is also true in many of the accounts related to Panhu.

claims.statement: The worm then became a dog, Panhu, who in some versions had five-colored fur; the king offered his daughter in marriage to anyone who would bring him the head of his enemy, and Panhu accomplished it.
claims.statement_id: Cacing itu kemudian menjadi anjing bernama Panhu yang dalam sebagian versi berbulu lima warna; raja menawarkan putrinya kepada siapa pun yang membawa kepala musuhnya, dan hal itu dilakukan oleh Panhu.
claims.quote: The worm then turned into a dog, Panhu, who in some versions had five colored fur. The king offered to marry his daughter to anybody that would present him with the head of his enemy. This was accomplished by Panhu.

claims.statement: Accounts vary, but eventually Panhu and the princess had six sons and six daughters who became the famous 12 clans of Chinese mythology.
claims.statement_id: Catatan berbeda-beda, tetapi akhirnya Panhu dan sang putri memiliki enam putra dan enam putri yang menjadi 12 klan terkenal dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
claims.quote: Accounts vary, but eventually Panhu and the princess had six sons and six daughters who became the famous 12 clans of Chinese mythology.

claims.statement: In modern times, Panhu has been worshiped by the She and Yao peoples as "King Pan".
claims.statement_id: Pada masa kini, Panhu dipuja oleh orang She dan orang Yao sebagai "Raja Pan".
claims.quote: In modern times, Panhu has been worshiped by the She people and Yao people as "King Pan".

claims.statement: This is the origin of Panhu's name, which literally means "plate gourd".
claims.statement_id: Inilah asal nama Panhu, yang secara harfiah berarti "labu piring".
claims.quote: This is the origin of Panhu's name, which literally means "plate gourd".

claims.statement: The Panhu myth is an important origin myth for various ethnic groups.
claims.statement_id: Mitos Panhu merupakan mitos asal-usul yang penting bagi berbagai kelompok etnis.
claims.quote: The Panhu myth is an important origin myth for various ethnic groups.

claims.statement: In this classical text, Gaoxin (高辛氏) is troubled by raids from the Quanrong (犬戎) and offers gold, towns, and his youngest daughter to anyone who brings the head of General Wu (吳將軍) of the Quanrong.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks klasik ini, Gaoxin (高辛氏) kewalahan oleh serangan Quanrong (犬戎) dan menawarkan emas, kota, dan putri bungsunya kepada siapa pun yang membawa kepala Jenderal Wu (吳將軍) dari Quanrong.
claims.quote: 昔高辛氏有犬戎之寇，帝患其侵暴，而征伐不克。乃訪募天下，有能得犬戎之將吳將軍頭者，購黃金千鎰，邑萬家，又妻以少女。

claims.statement: The emperor then had a dog with five-colored fur named Panhu (槃瓠); after the order was issued, Panhu carried a human head to the palace gate, and the ministers found it was General Wu's head.
claims.statement_id: Pada saat itu sang kaisar memiliki seekor anjing berbulu lima warna bernama Panhu (槃瓠); setelah titah diumumkan, Panhu membawa sebuah kepala manusia ke istana, dan para menteri mendapati itu kepala Jenderal Wu.
claims.quote: 時帝有畜狗，其毛五采，名曰槃瓠。下令之後，槃瓠遂銜人頭造闕下，群臣怪而診之，乃吳將軍首也。

claims.statement: Having no choice, the emperor gave his daughter to Panhu (槃瓠); Panhu carried her on his back into the Southern Mountain (南山) and stayed in a stone chamber in a perilous place no one reached.
claims.statement_id: Karena terpaksa, sang kaisar menikahkan putrinya dengan Panhu (槃瓠); Panhu menggendong sang putri ke Gunung Selatan (南山) dan tinggal di sebuah ruang batu di tempat yang berbahaya dan tidak dijejaki orang.
claims.quote: 帝不得已，乃以女配槃瓠。槃瓠得女，負而走入南山，止石室中。所處險絶，人迹不至。

claims.statement: After three years twelve children were born, six sons and six daughters; after Panhu (槃瓠) died they married one another, wove tree bark, dyed it with plant seeds, liked five-colored clothes, and cut garments with tail shapes.
claims.statement_id: Setelah tiga tahun lahir dua belas anak, enam putra dan enam putri; sesudah Panhu (槃瓠) meninggal mereka saling menjadi suami istri, menenun kulit kayu, mewarnainya dengan biji tumbuhan, menyukai pakaian lima warna, dan menjahit pakaian berbentuk ekor.
claims.quote: 經三年，生子一十二人，六男六女。槃瓠死後，因自相夫妻。織績木皮，染以草實，好五色衣服。製裁皆有尾形。

claims.statement: Their descendants later multiplied and were called the Manyi (蠻夷); the text calls them seemingly foolish outside but shrewd within, attached to their land and old ways, and says they are the Man of Changsha and Wuling (長沙武陵蠻).
claims.statement_id: Keturunan mereka kemudian berkembang dan disebut Manyi (蠻夷); teks itu menyebut mereka tampak bodoh di luar tetapi cerdik di dalam, setia pada tanah dan kebiasaan lama, dan menyatakan bahwa merekalah suku Man di Changsha dan Wuling (長沙武陵蠻).
claims.quote: 其後滋蔓，號曰蠻夷。外癡內黠，安土重舊。 ... 今長沙武陵蠻是也。

claims.statement: Panlong is an aquatic Chinese mythological dragon resembling jiaolong and also serving as an artistic motif.
claims.statement_id: Panlong adalah naga air mitologi Tiongkok yang menyerupai jiaolong dan juga menjadi motif seni.
claims.quote: Panlong (simplified Chinese: 蟠龙; traditional Chinese: 蟠龍; pinyin: pánlóng; Wade–Giles: p'an-lung; lit. "coiled dragon") is an aquatic dragon resembling a jiaolong 蛟龍 "river dragon; crocodile" in Chinese mythology, an ancient motif in Chinese art, and a proper name.

claims.statement: The Huainanzi records Panlong as a bronze-decoration style.
claims.statement_id: Huainanzi mencatat Panlong sebagai gaya hiasan perunggu.
claims.quote: Chinese classic texts began using panlong in the Han dynasty (206 BCE – 220 CE). The (2nd century BCE) Huainanzi first records panlong as a decorative style on Chinese bronzes.

claims.statement: The Fangyan (方言) dictionary of Yang Xiong defined panlong 蟠龍 as a "coiled dragon": dragons which do not yet ascend to heaven are called p'an-lung.
claims.statement_id: Kamus Fangyan (方言) karya Yang Xiong mendefinisikan panlong 蟠龍 sebagai "naga melingkar": naga yang belum naik ke langit disebut p'an-lung.
claims.quote: The materialist philosopher Yang Xiong (53 BCE – 18 CE) used both panlong and longpan. His Fangyan 方言 "Regional Speech" dictionary defined panlong 蟠龍 "coiled/curled dragon", "Dragons which do not yet ascend to heaven [cf. tianlong "heavenly dragon"] are called p'an-lung."

claims.statement: The Biji manzhi (碧雞漫志) by Wang Zhuo (王灼) describes using panlong dragons in sympathetic magic for rainfall: a mirror adorned on its back with a "coiled dragon" (盤龍) is said to have been worshipped, or used magically, to cause rain.
claims.statement_id: Biji manzhi (碧雞漫志) karya Wang Zhuo (王灼) menggambarkan pemakaian naga panlong dalam sihir simpatetik untuk hujan: cermin yang punggungnya dihiasi "naga melingkar" (盤龍) dikatakan dipuja, atau digunakan secara magis, untuk mendatangkan hujan.
claims.quote: The (12th century CE) Song dynasty Biji manzhi 碧雞漫志 "Random Jottings from the Green Rooster Quarter" by Wang Zhuo 王灼 describes using panlong dragons in sympathetic magic for rainfall, "where a mirror, adorned on the backside with a "coiled dragon", p'an lung, 盤龍, is said to have been worshipped (rather used in a magical way) in order to cause rain."

claims.statement: The Shangshu dazhuan (尚書大傳) commentary to the Classic of History parallels panlong with jiaoyu (鮫魚) and says the "coiled dragon" was greatly trusted in its lair.
claims.statement_id: Komentar Shangshu dazhuan (尚書大傳) atas Classic of History memadankan panlong dengan jiaoyu (鮫魚) dan menyebut "naga melingkar" itu sangat dipercaya di sarangnya.
claims.quote: Shangshu dazhuan 尚書大傳 ... commentary to the Classic of History parallels panlong and jiaoyu 鮫魚 ... was greatly trusted in its lair

claims.statement: A classical text describing the decoration of great bells, tripods, and precious vessels lists the 蟠龍 (coiled dragon) motif linked in a series (連組) alongside the sleeping rhinoceros (寢兕) and the crouching tiger (伏虎).
claims.statement_id: Sebuah teks klasik yang menyebut hiasan lonceng besar, kuali tripod, dan bejana berharga mencantumkan motif 蟠龍 (naga melingkar) yang berangkai (連組) di samping badak tidur (寢兕) dan harimau mendekam (伏虎).
claims.quote: 大鐘鼎，美重器，華蟲疏鏤，以相繆紾，寢兕伏虎，蟠龍連組，焜昱錯眩，照耀輝煌

claims.statement: Shangyang is a Chinese mythological bird capable of predicting rain.
claims.statement_id: Shangyang adalah burung mitologi Tiongkok yang dapat meramalkan hujan.
claims.quote: The Shangyang (商羊), (or shang yang) in Chinese mythology was a rainbird (i.e. it could predict rain). It was one of several important mythical birds in this tradition. The Shangyang was particularly associated with the Lord of Rain, Yu Shi. Once, the Shangyang was said to have visited the royal court of Qi, where it danced on one leg.

claims.statement: This creature is associated with Yu Shi, the Lord of Rain.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini dikaitkan dengan Yu Shi, Penguasa Hujan.
claims.quote: The Shangyang (商羊), (or shang yang) in Chinese mythology was a rainbird (i.e. it could predict rain). It was one of several important mythical birds in this tradition. The Shangyang was particularly associated with the Lord of Rain, Yu Shi. Once, the Shangyang was said to have visited the royal court of Qi, where it danced on one leg.

claims.statement: One account describes it dancing on one leg at the court of Qi.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah kisah menyebutnya menari dengan satu kaki di istana Qi.
claims.quote: The Shangyang (商羊), (or shang yang) in Chinese mythology was a rainbird (i.e. it could predict rain). It was one of several important mythical birds in this tradition. The Shangyang was particularly associated with the Lord of Rain, Yu Shi. Once, the Shangyang was said to have visited the royal court of Qi, where it danced on one leg.

claims.statement: Confucius, who was familiar with the Shangyang, predicted heavy rain and advised the people to dig drainage channels and build dikes; by following this advice Qi avoided the flood that followed, while other states that ignored it were heavily damaged.
claims.statement_id: Konfusius, yang mengenal Shangyang, meramalkan hujan lebat dan menasihati rakyat menggali saluran dan membangun tanggul; dengan mengikuti nasihat itu Qi terhindar dari bencana banjir yang menyusul, sedangkan negara lain yang mengabaikannya rusak parah.
claims.quote: Confucius, who was familiar with the Shangyang, predicted heavy rain and advised the people to dig drainage channels and build dikes. By following the sage's advice, Qi avoided the disaster caused by a subsequent flood, while other states that ignored this advice were heavily damaged.

claims.statement: This legendary incident has often been used to illustrate the foolishness of those who ignore wise advice.
claims.statement_id: Peristiwa legendaris ini sering dipakai untuk menggambarkan kebodohan orang yang mengabaikan nasihat bijak.
claims.quote: This legendary incident has often been used to illustrate the foolishness of those who ignore wise advice.

claims.statement: The mythographer Lihui Yang instead associates Yu Shi with the Bi Fang bird.
claims.statement_id: Ahli mitografi Lihui Yang justru mengaitkan Yu Shi dengan burung Bi Fang.
claims.quote: Mythographer Lihui Yang associates Yu Shi with the Bi Fang bird, instead.

claims.statement: In this classical text, a one-legged bird (一足之鳥) flies into the court of Qi (齊), lands before the hall, and hops with spread wings; the Marquis of Qi (齊侯) is astonished and sends an envoy to Lu (魯) to ask Confucius (孔子).
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks klasik ini, seekor burung berkaki satu (一足之鳥) terbang ke istana negeri Qi (齊), mendarat di depan balai, dan melompat dengan sayap terkembang; Marquis Qi (齊侯) heran lalu mengutus orang ke negeri Lu (魯) untuk bertanya kepada Konfusius (孔子).
claims.quote: 齊有一足之鳥，飛集於宮朝，下止於殿前，舒翅而跳。齊侯大怪之，使使聘魯，問孔子。

claims.statement: Confucius (孔子) says the bird is named Shangyang (商羊), a water omen (水祥); children once bent one leg, knitted their brows, and hopped singing "Heaven will send great rain, the Shangyang dances", and now that Qi has it, the sign has arrived.
claims.statement_id: Konfusius (孔子) berkata bahwa burung itu bernama Shangyang (商羊), pertanda air (水祥); dulu anak-anak menekuk satu kaki, mengerutkan alis, melompat sambil bernyanyi "Langit akan menurunkan hujan lebat, Shangyang menari", dan kini Qi memilikinya sehingga pertandanya telah tiba.
claims.quote: 孔子曰：「此鳥名曰商羊，水祥也。昔童兒有屈其一腳，振訊兩眉，而跳且謠曰：『天將大雨，商羊鼓舞。』今齊有之，其應至矣。」

claims.statement: The people were told urgently to repair ditches and dikes because a great flood was coming; soon heavy rain fell, water overflowed many states and harmed the people, but only Qi (齊), which had prepared, was not ruined.
claims.statement_id: Rakyat segera diberi tahu agar membenahi parit dan memperbaiki tanggul karena banjir besar akan datang; tak lama kemudian hujan deras turun, air meluap ke berbagai negara dan melukai penduduk, tetapi hanya Qi (齊) yang siap dan tidak rusak.
claims.quote: 急告民趨治溝渠，修堤防，將有大水為災。頃之大霖雨，水溢泛諸國，傷害民人。唯齊有備，不敗。

claims.statement: Shunfeng'er is a Chinese sea and door god guarding Mazu temples with Qianliyan.
claims.statement_id: Shunfeng'er adalah dewa laut dan pintu Tiongkok yang menjaga kuil Mazu bersama Qianliyan.
claims.quote: Shunfeng'er is a Chinese sea and door god. He usually appears with Qianliyan as a guardian of the temples of the sea goddess Mazu.

claims.statement: His name refers to hearing sounds carried by the wind.
claims.statement_id: Namanya mengacu pada kemampuan mendengar suara yang dibawa angin.
claims.quote: The name "Shunfeng'er" literally means "Wind Accompanying Ears" in reference to his ability to hear any sound carried upon the wind.

claims.statement: Shunfeng Er and Shen Feng Er are alternative spellings of his name.
claims.statement_id: Shunfeng Er dan Shen Feng Er merupakan ejaan lain namanya.
claims.quote: It also appears as Shunfeng Er and Shen Feng Er. His partner Qianliyan's name similarly means "Sharp-Eyed" or "All-Seeing".

claims.statement: In the Ming period, he was also known as Shi Kuang.
claims.statement_id: Pada zaman Ming, ia juga dikenal sebagai Shi Kuang.
claims.quote: Under the Ming, Shunfeng'er was also known as Shi Kuang. He is also sometimes known as Wanli'er, which has similar meaning, as the Chinese word wàn—like the English "myriad"—simultaneously means the number 10,000 and "innumerable" or "uncountably vast".

claims.statement: Journey to the West presents him as the personified ears of the Jade Emperor.
claims.statement_id: Journey to the West menampilkannya sebagai personifikasi telinga Kaisar Giok.
claims.quote: Shunfeng'er is first attested in the early-16th century novel Journey to the West, where he appears as the personified form of the Taoist Jade Emperor's ears and one of his lieutenants. There is, however, an earlier depiction of him in a Sichuan cave which has been dated to the Southern Song.

claims.statement: Shunfeng'er's sharp hearing is used to help sailors tell favorable winds from coming storms; in some accounts he can hear everything in the world however quietly spoken, and was therefore also worshipped as a witness and guarantor of oaths and contracts.
claims.statement_id: Pendengaran Shunfeng'er yang tajam dipakai untuk membantu pelaut membedakan angin yang baik dari badai yang akan datang; dalam sebagian kisah ia mampu mendengar segalanya di dunia, sepelan apa pun, sehingga juga dipuja sebagai saksi dan penjamin sumpah dan kontrak.
claims.quote: Shunfeng'er's sharp hearing is employed to help sailors distinguish favorable winds from coming storms. In some accounts, he is capable of hearing everything in the world, no matter how quietly spoken, and was therefore also worshipped as a witness and guarantor of oaths and contracts.

claims.statement: Shunfeng'er is most often portrayed as a demon defeated and tamed or befriended by the sea goddess Mazu.
claims.statement_id: Shunfeng'er paling sering digambarkan sebagai iblis yang dikalahkan dan dijinakkan atau diajak berteman oleh dewi laut Mazu.
claims.quote: Shunfeng'er is most often portrayed as a demon defeated and tamed or befriended by the sea goddess Mazu.

claims.statement: By one account, he and Qianliyan appeared off Meizhou Island during a storm and were defeated by Mazu's magical silk scarf, which blew clouds of sand into their ears and eyes; after submitting they pledged loyalty when she healed the damage she had caused.
claims.statement_id: Menurut satu kisah, ia dan Qianliyan muncul di lepas pantai Pulau Meizhou saat badai dan dikalahkan oleh selendang sutra sakti Mazu yang meniupkan awan pasir ke telinga dan mata mereka; setelah tunduk, mereka berjanji setia ketika Mazu menyembuhkan luka yang ditimbulkannya.
claims.quote: By one account, he and Qianliyan appeared off Meizhou Island during a storm and were defeated by Mazu's magical silk scarf, which blew clouds of sand into their ears and eyes. After their submission, they pledged their loyalty when she kindly healed them of the damage she had caused them.

claims.statement: In another account the two were the brothers Gao Jue and Gao Ming, ruthless generals who fell at Peach Blossom Mountain and subsequently haunted it as demons.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah lain, keduanya adalah saudara Gao Jue dan Gao Ming, jenderal kejam yang gugur di Gunung Peach Blossom dan kemudian menghantuinya sebagai iblis.
claims.quote: In another, the two were the brothers Gao Jue and Gao Ming. Ruthless generals, they fell at Peach Blossom Mountain and subsequently haunted it as demons.

claims.statement: Shunfeng'er typically appears as a red- or brown-skinned demon cupping a hand to one of his ears, and occasionally with three heads and six arms.
claims.statement_id: Shunfeng'er biasanya digambarkan sebagai iblis berkulit merah atau cokelat yang menangkupkan tangan ke salah satu telinganya, dan kadang-kadang bertiga kepala dan berlengan enam.
claims.quote: Shunfeng'er typically appears as a red- or brown-skinned demon cupping a hand to one of his ears. He also occasionally appears with three heads and six arms.

claims.statement: In folk myth, the two guardian gods who observe and listen to the affairs of the world for Mazu (媽祖) are 千里眼 (also called 金精將軍) and 順風耳 (also called 水精將軍).
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitos rakyat, dua dewa pengawal yang mengawasi dan mendengar urusan dunia bagi Mazu (媽祖) adalah 千里眼 (juga disebut 金精將軍) dan 順風耳 (juga disebut 水精將軍).
claims.quote: 在民間的神話傳說中，替媽祖察聽世情的兩大駕前護衛神分別為千里眼（又稱金精將軍）與順風耳（又稱水精將軍）。

claims.statement: In Mazu (媽祖) temples, 千里眼 and 順風耳 stand on Mazu's left and right; 順風耳 raises a hand to his ear in a listening pose, using his boundless hearing to scout everything in the world for Mazu, and the other hand holds a weapon.
claims.statement_id: Di kuil Mazu (媽祖), 千里眼 dan 順風耳 berdiri di kiri dan kanan Mazu; 順風耳 mengangkat tangan ke samping telinga dalam sikap mendengar, memakai pendengarannya yang tak terbatas untuk menyelidiki segala hal di dunia bagi Mazu, dan tangan yang lain memegang senjata.
claims.quote: 在媽祖廟裡，千里眼和順風耳分別站立於媽祖的左右兩側 ... 而順風耳則手舉至側耳做聽音狀的姿態，以其無遠弗屆的聽力，為媽祖偵聽世上的一切事物。祂們的另一手則持有兵器。

claims.statement: Legends about 千里眼 and 順風耳 differ, but generally they were originally spirit-monsters on Peach Blossom Mountain (桃花山) with fierce faces who frightened residents and often disturbed the area and harmed the people, until Mazu (媽祖) subdued them and they became her attendant generals.
claims.statement_id: Legenda tentang 千里眼 dan 順風耳 berbeda-beda, tetapi pada umumnya keduanya semula adalah siluman di Gunung Peach Blossom (桃花山) yang berwajah garang, menakuti penduduk, dan sering mengganggu daerah itu serta merugikan rakyat, hingga akhirnya ditaklukkan Mazu (媽祖) dan menjadi jenderal pengiringnya.
claims.quote: 關於千里眼和順風耳的傳說不一，總的來說，祂們原來是在桃花山上的妖精，不僅面貌猙獰，使居民恐懼外，更時常擾亂地方、為害百姓。最後為媽祖收伏，成為隨駕將軍。

claims.statement: In Mazu (媽祖) processions, besides Mazu's palanquin one always sees two great generals, one green and one red, who are Mazu's left and right protectors, 千里眼 and 順風耳.
claims.statement_id: Dalam arak-arakan Mazu (媽祖), selain tandu Mazu selalu tampak dua jenderal besar, satu hijau dan satu merah, yaitu pelindung kiri dan kanan Mazu: 千里眼 dan 順風耳.
claims.quote: 在媽祖出巡的陣頭中，除了媽祖鑾轎外，我們總會看見一綠一紅的大將軍，這就是媽祖的左右護法──千里眼和順風耳。

claims.statement: This classical text says the evil creature is the peach spirit and willow ghost of Mount Qipan (棋盤山), and that in the Xuanyuan temple (軒轅廟) there are clay ghost attendants named 千里眼 and 順風耳; the two monsters borrow their spiritual power so that the eyes can see a thousand li and the ears can hear a thousand li, but they cannot see or hear beyond a thousand li.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks klasik ini disebut bahwa makhluk jahat itu adalah roh persik dan hantu willow dari Gunung Qipan (棋盤山), dan di kuil Xuanyuan (軒轅廟) di sana ada utusan hantu dari tanah liat bernama 千里眼 dan 順風耳; kedua siluman itu meminjam daya gaibnya sehingga mata dapat melihat seribu li dan telinga dapat mendengar seribu li, tetapi tidak dapat melihat atau mendengar melampaui seribu li.
claims.quote: 此業障是棋盤山桃精、柳鬼 ... 今棋盤山有軒轅廟，廟內有泥塑鬼使，名曰千里眼，順風耳；二怪托其靈氣，目能觀看千里，耳能詳聽千里；千里之外，不能視聽也。

claims.statement: In this classical text, Jiang Ziya (姜子牙) is advised to send people to Mount Qipan (棋盤山) to dig up and burn the peach and willow roots and to smash the clay bodies of the two ghosts in the Xuanyuan temple (軒轅廟) in order to cut the root of their spiritual power.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks klasik ini, Jiang Ziya (姜子牙) disarankan mengirim orang ke Gunung Qipan (棋盤山) untuk menggali akar persik dan willow lalu membakarnya, dan menghancurkan tubuh tanah liat kedua hantu di kuil Xuanyuan (軒轅廟) guna memutus akar daya gaib mereka.
claims.quote: 你可叫姜子牙著人往棋盤山去，將桃、柳根盤掘挖，用火焚盡；將軒轅廟二鬼泥身打碎，以絕其靈氣之根

claims.statement: Tam Kung is a sea deity worshipped in Hong Kong and Macau.
claims.statement_id: Tam Kung adalah dewa laut yang dipuja di Hong Kong dan Makau.
claims.quote: Tam Kung (Chinese: 譚公; lit. 'Lord Tam') or Tam Tai Sin (譚大仙) is a sea deity worshiped in Hong Kong and Macau.

claims.statement: Legend credits him with forecasting weather and healing from childhood.
claims.statement_id: Legenda memberinya kemampuan meramalkan cuaca dan menyembuhkan sejak kecil.
claims.quote: In Chinese folk legends, Tam Kung was one of gods who could forecast the weather. He was born in Huizhou Prefecture. It was said that he could cure patients in his childhood.

claims.statement: The tale says he becomes immortal at twenty on Nine-dragon Mountain.
claims.statement_id: Kisah menyebut ia menjadi makhluk abadi pada usia dua puluh di Gunung Sembilan Naga.
claims.quote: Tam Kung became an immortal in heaven at the age of twenty in the Nine-dragon Mountain in Huizhou.

claims.statement: Residents funded construction of the Shau Kei Wan temple in 1905.
claims.statement_id: Penduduk mendanai pembangunan kuil di Shau Kei Wan pada 1905.
claims.quote: The Tam Kung Sin Shing Temple (譚公仙聖廟) is located along Tam Kung Temple Road, at the northern end of Shau Kei Wan Main Street East, in A Kung Ngam, Shau Kei Wan. It was originally a small shrine. Local people raised money to construct it in 1905 and reconstructed it many times afterwards.

claims.statement: The Chinese Temples Committee has managed the temple since 1928.
claims.statement_id: Komite Kuil Tiongkok mengelola kuil tersebut sejak 1928.
claims.quote: The temple has been managed by the Chinese Temples Committee since 1928. The temple is a former Grade I historic building. It is a Grade III historic building since April 2013.

claims.statement: The Temples Committee describes Tam Kung as youthful and credits him with commanding wind and rain.
claims.statement_id: Komite Kuil menyebut penggambaran Tam Kung sebagai sosok muda berwajah segar dan memiliki kemampuan mengatur angin serta hujan.
claims.quote: Tam Kung was originally a native of Huizhou (惠州) in Guangdong Province (廣東省) during Yuan Dynasty (元朝). He is usually portrayed as being young and having a fresh face. When he was 13 years old, he had already possessed supernatural powers to command the wind and rain, cure sickness, and forecast weather. His ability made him a popular deity.

claims.statement: He was officially deified during the Qing dynasty, and people whose ancestral home is Huizhou or Chaoshan in Guangdong province worship him most devoutly.
claims.statement_id: Ia diangkat resmi menjadi dewa pada masa Dinasti Qing, dan orang yang berasal dari Huizhou atau Chaoshan, Provinsi Guangdong, paling tekun memujanya.
claims.quote: He was officially deified during the Qing dynasty. People whose ancestral home are in Huizhou or Chaoshan of Guangdong province worship Tam Kung most sincerely.

claims.statement: A big rock in front of the Shau Kei Wan temple is believed to be Tam Kung’s magic stamp.
claims.statement_id: Batu besar di depan kuil Shau Kei Wan dipercaya sebagai cap sakti (magic stamp) Tam Kung.
claims.quote: There is a big rock in front of the temple and is believed to be Tam Kung's magic stamp.

claims.statement: On Tam Kung’s birthday (8th day of the 4th month of the Chinese calendar), a celebration is held with a "kung fu" show, a parade and a dragon dance.
claims.statement_id: Pada hari lahir Tam Kung (hari ke-8 bulan ke-4 kalender Tionghoa) diadakan perayaan dengan pertunjukan "kung fu", pawai, dan tari naga.
claims.quote: On the birthday of Tam Kung (8th day of the 4th month in Chinese calendar), they will have a celebration and play a so-called "kung fu" show which is a major part of the celebration. A parade and dragon dance are also held on this occasion.

claims.statement: According to a story, Tam Kung appeared to a young boy in a dream and guided him to the present Happy Valley site, regarded as chosen by the deity itself.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kisah, Tam Kung menampakkan diri dalam mimpi seorang anak laki-laki dan menuntunnya ke lokasi kuil Happy Valley yang sekarang, yang dianggap dipilih sendiri oleh dewa itu.
claims.quote: According to a story, Tam Kung appeared to a young boy in a dream and guided him to the present site, which was regarded as selected by the deity for the new location of the temple.

claims.statement: In Victoria, British Columbia, Canada, there is also a Tam Kung temple, erected in 1876.
claims.statement_id: Di Victoria, British Columbia, Kanada, juga ada kuil Tam Kung yang didirikan pada 1876.
claims.quote: In Victoria, BC, Canada, there is also a temple to the deity, Tam Kung. The temple was erected in 1876.

claims.statement: In the past, stonecutters from Huizhou came to Hong Kong and brought their belief in Tam Kung from their hometown.
claims.statement_id: Dahulu para pemotong batu dari Huizhou datang ke Hong Kong dan membawa kepercayaan kepada Tam Kung dari kampung halamannya.
claims.quote: In the past, stonecutters from Huizhou came to Hong Kong and brought their belief in Tam Kung from hometown.

claims.statement: Teng, or Tengshe, is a flying dragon of Chinese mythology.
claims.statement_id: Teng atau Tengshe adalah naga terbang dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
claims.quote: Teng (Chinese: 螣; pinyin: téng; Wade–Giles: tʻêng) or Tengshe (traditional Chinese: 螣蛇／騰蛇; simplified Chinese: 螣蛇／腾蛇; pinyin: téngshé; Wade–Giles: tʻêng-shê; lit. 'soaring snake') is a flying dragon in Chinese mythology.

claims.statement: Tengshe may denote a flying-dragon snake or soaring snake.
claims.statement_id: Sebutan Tengshe dapat bermakna ular naga terbang atau ular yang melayang.
claims.quote: This legendary creature's names include teng (螣; "a flying dragon") and tengshe (螣蛇; "flying-dragon snake" or 騰蛇; "soaring snake").

claims.statement: The teng character combines a phonetic component with an insect component.
claims.statement_id: Aksara teng menggabungkan unsur fonetik dengan unsur serangga.
claims.quote: The Chinese character 螣 for teng graphically combines a phonetic element of zhen (朕) with the "insect radical" 虫. This radical is typically used in characters for insects, worms, reptiles, and dragons, such as in shen (蜃; "a sea-monster dragon") or jiao (蛟; "an aquatic dragon").

claims.statement: Guo Pu's Erya commentary describes it drifting through clouds and mist.
claims.statement_id: Komentar Guo Pu atas Erya menggambarkannya melayang dalam awan dan kabut.
claims.quote: The (3rd–2nd centuries BCE) Erya dictionary (16) defines teng (螣) as tengshe (螣蛇; "teng-snake"), and Guo Pu's commentary glosses it as a "[飛龍; feilong] flying dragon that drifts in the clouds and mist".

claims.statement: From the original "flying dragon; flying serpent" meaning, tengshe acquired three further meanings: "an asterism" in traditional Chinese star names, "a battle formation" in Chinese military history, and "lines above the mouth" in physiognomy.
claims.statement_id: Dari makna asli "naga terbang; ular terbang", tengshe memperoleh tiga makna tambahan: "rasi bintang" dalam nama bintang tradisional Tiongkok, "formasi tempur" dalam sejarah militer Tiongkok, dan "garis di atas mulut" dalam ilmu fisiognomi.
claims.quote: From the original "flying dragon; flying serpent" denotation, tengshe acquired three additional meanings: "an asterism" in Traditional Chinese star names, "a battle formation" in Chinese military history, and "lines above the mouth" in physiognomy.

claims.statement: The Confucianist Xunzi first records the Classical Chinese idiom tengshe wuzu er fei, "flying dragon is without feet yet flies", which figuratively means "success results from concentrating on one's abilities".
claims.statement_id: Xunzi, seorang Konfusianis, pertama kali mencatat idiom Tionghoa klasik tengshe wuzu er fei, "naga terbang tidak berkaki namun terbang", yang secara kiasan berarti "keberhasilan datang dari memusatkan diri pada kemampuan sendiri".
claims.quote: Confucianist Xunzi ... first records the Classical Chinese idiom tengshe wuzu er fei ... "flying dragon is without feet yet flies", which figuratively means "success results from concentrating on one's abilities".

claims.statement: In the Huainanzi, the ascending snake (tengshe) can drift in the mist yet is endangered by the centipede.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Huainanzi, ular yang naik (tengshe) dapat melayang di dalam kabut, namun terancam oleh kelabang.
claims.quote: Huainanzi uses both tengshe graphic variants ... The ascending snake can drift in the mist, yet it is endangered by the centipede.

claims.statement: The Bencao Gangmu (1578) mentions flying snakes without feet such as the 螣蛇 (T'eng She); its commentary says the t'eng-she changes into a dragon, and this divine snake can ride the clouds and fly over a thousand miles.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Bencao Gangmu (1578), ular terbang tanpa kaki seperti 螣蛇 (T'eng She) disebut; komentarnya menyatakan bahwa t'eng-she berubah menjadi naga, ular ilahi ini dapat menunggangi awan dan terbang lebih dari seribu mil.
claims.quote: The (1578 CE) Bencao Gangmu ... "There are flying snakes without feet such as the 螣蛇 (T'eng She)." ... The t'eng-she changes into a dragon. This divine snake can ride upon the clouds and fly about over a thousand miles.

claims.statement: Shenzi (慎子) says the flying dragon (飛龍) rides the clouds and the rising snake (騰蛇) wanders in the mist, but when clouds disperse and mist clears, the dragon and snake become the same as earthworms and ants because they lose what they ride.
claims.statement_id: Shenzi (慎子) berkata bahwa naga terbang (飛龍) menunggangi awan dan ular terbang (騰蛇) mengembara di kabut, tetapi ketika awan bubar dan kabut cerah, naga dan ular itu sama saja dengan cacing dan semut karena kehilangan apa yang ditungganginya.
claims.quote: 慎子曰：飛龍乘雲，騰蛇遊霧，雲罷霧霽，而龍蛇與螾螘同矣，則失其所乘也。

claims.statement: Tianma is a flying horse in Chinese folklore, with wings possibly understood metaphorically.
claims.statement_id: Tianma adalah kuda terbang dalam cerita rakyat Tiongkok, dengan sayap yang mungkin bersifat kiasan.
claims.quote: Tianma (天馬 Tiānmǎ, "heavenly horse") was a winged (perhaps metaphorically) flying horse in Chinese folklore.

claims.statement: Its portrayal sometimes includes composite features such as dragon scales.
claims.statement_id: Penggambarannya kadang memiliki ciri campuran seperti sisik naga.
claims.quote: The Tianma is a flying horse that was sometimes depicted with chimerical features such as dragon scales and was at times attributed the ability to sweat blood, possibly inspired by the parasite Parafilaria multipapillosa, which infected the highly sought-after Ferghana horse (大宛馬), sometimes conflated with Tianma.

claims.statement: The blood-sweating attributed to Tianma may be inspired by parasites on Ferghana horses.
claims.statement_id: Keringat darah yang dilekatkan pada Tianma mungkin terinspirasi parasit pada kuda Ferghana.

claims.statement: In Western Zhou usage, Tianma also referred to a constellation.
claims.statement_id: Dalam penggunaan zaman Zhou Barat, Tianma juga merujuk pada rasi.
claims.quote: In the Western Zhou Empire, Tianma referred to a constellation. Tianma is also associated with Emperor Wu of Han, an aficionado of the Central Asian horse, and the famous poet Li Bo. The bronze statue Flying Horse of Gansu is a well-known example.

claims.quote: Tianma, the flying horse, is clearly connected to Pegasus from the Western Han dynasty artwork and in the Tang dynasty sources, as coming from Hellenized Central Asia.

claims.statement: In this classical history text, the emperor (天子) consults a text that says "divine horses will come from the northwest"; good Wusun (烏孫) horses are named "天馬", and after obtaining stronger blood-sweating (汗血) Dayuan (大宛) horses, the Wusun horses are renamed "西極" and the Dayuan horses are named "天馬".
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks sejarah klasik ini, sang kaisar (天子) membuka naskah dan memperoleh bunyi "kuda dewa akan datang dari barat laut"; kuda Wusun (烏孫) yang baik dinamai "天馬", dan setelah mendapat kuda Dayuan (大宛) yang berkeringat darah (汗血) yang lebih gagah, kuda Wusun dinamai ulang "西極" dan kuda Dayuan dinamai "天馬".
claims.quote: 初，天子發書易，云「神馬當從西北來」。得烏孫馬好，名曰「天馬」。及得大宛汗血馬，益壯，更名烏孫馬曰「西極」，名大宛馬曰「天馬」云。

claims.statement: This classical history text says Dayuan (大宛) lies southwest of the Xiongnu and due west of Han, has many fine horses that sweat blood (馬汗血), and that their ancestor was the offspring of the heavenly horse (天馬子).
claims.statement_id: Teks sejarah klasik ini menyebut Dayuan (大宛) terletak di barat daya Xiongnu dan tepat di barat Han, memiliki banyak kuda bagus yang berkeringat darah (馬汗血), dan leluhurnya dikatakan keturunan kuda langit (天馬子).
claims.quote: 大宛在匈奴西南，在漢正西，去漢可萬里 ... 多善馬，馬汗血，其先天馬子也。

claims.statement: A hymn in this classical text says the heavenly horse (天馬) descends with red sweat (赤汗) and ochre-colored foam, crosses ten thousand li (萬里), and has the dragon as friend (龍為友); its annotation says it was composed in the third year of Yuanshou (元狩三年) when a horse was born in the Wowa water (渥洼水).
claims.statement_id: Sebuah himne dalam teks klasik ini menyebut kuda langit (天馬) turun dengan keringat merah (赤汗) dan busa mengalir kemerahan, melintasi sepuluh ribu li (萬里), dan berkawan dengan naga (龍為友); catatan anotasinya menyebut himne itu dibuat pada tahun ketiga Yuanshou (元狩三年) ketika seekor kuda lahir di air Wowa (渥洼水).
claims.quote: 太一況，天馬下，霑赤汗，沬流赭。志俶儻，精權奇，逦浮雲，晻上馳。體容與，迣萬里，今安匹，龍為友。〈元狩三年馬生渥洼水中作。〉

claims.statement: Another hymn says the heavenly horse (天馬) comes from the far west (西極), crosses the flowing sands, emerges from spring water, has a tiger-like spine (虎脊), and transforms like a ghost or spirit (化若鬼).
claims.statement_id: Himne lain menyebut kuda langit (天馬) datang dari ujung barat (西極) melintasi pasir yang mengalir, muncul dari air mata air, berpunggung seperti harimau (虎脊), dan perubahannya seperti hantu (化若鬼).
claims.quote: 天馬徠，從西極，涉流沙，九夷服。天馬徠，出泉水，虎脊兩，化若鬼。

claims.statement: The next hymn says the heavenly horse (天馬) comes toward Kunlun (昆侖), acts as the dragon's matchmaker or guide (龍之媒), roams the gate of heaven (閶闔) and views the jade terrace (玉臺); its annotation says it was composed in the fourth year of Taichu (太初四年) when the king of Dayuan (宛王) was executed and Dayuan horses were obtained.
claims.statement_id: Himne berikutnya menyebut kuda langit (天馬) datang menuju Kunlun (昆侖), menjadi perantara bagi naga (龍之媒), mengembara di gerbang langit (閶闔) dan memandang teras giok (玉臺); anotasinya menyebut himne itu dibuat pada tahun keempat Taichu (太初四年) ketika raja Dayuan (宛王) dihukum dan kuda Dayuan diperoleh.
claims.quote: 天馬徠，開遠門，竦予身，逝昆侖。天馬徠，龍之媒，游閶闔，觀玉臺。〈太初四年誅宛王獲宛馬作。〉

claims.statement: Yuqiang is a deity of the north sea and wind in Chinese mythology.
claims.statement_id: Yuqiang adalah dewa laut utara dan angin dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
claims.quote: Yuqiang (Chinese: 禺强, alternatively Yujiang 禺疆 or Yujing 禺京), in Chinese mythology is one of the descendants of Huang Di, the "Yellow Emperor". Yuqiang was also the god of the north sea and a wind god. His father was Yuhao, another sea god.

claims.statement: Yuqiang was also the god of the north sea and a wind god; his father was Yuhao, another sea god.
claims.statement_id: Yuqiang juga dewa laut utara dan dewa angin; ayahnya Yuhao, dewa laut lain.
claims.quote: Yuqiang was also the god of the north sea and a wind god. His father was Yuhao, another sea god.

claims.statement: Some Shanhaijing accounts give him a bird body and human face, with serpents supporting his feet in travel.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian catatan Shanhaijing memberikan tubuh burung dan wajah manusia dengan ular sebagai tunggangan kaki.
claims.quote: Some accounts (Shanhaijing chapters 8 and 17) describe Yuqiang as having the body of a bird and the face of a human being, with a serpent mount for each foot that facilitated his travels.

claims.statement: This classical text says 禺彊 (Yuqiang) of the north has a human face and bird body, wears two green snakes (青蛇) as earrings and treads on two green snakes.
claims.statement_id: Teks klasik ini menyebut 禺彊 (Yuqiang) di utara berwajah manusia dan bertubuh burung, dengan dua ular hijau (青蛇) sebagai anting dan menginjak dua ular hijau.
claims.quote: 有青獸焉，狀如虎，名曰羅羅。 ... 北方禺彊，人面鳥身，珥兩青蛇。踐兩青蛇。

claims.statement: Another classical text says that on an islet in the North Sea (北海) there is a god with a human face and bird body, with two green snakes (青蛇) at his ears and two red snakes (赤蛇) under his feet, named 禺彊 (Yuqiang); the preceding sentence mentions the Daner country (儋耳之國) of the Ren (任) surname, descended from Yuhao (禺號).
claims.statement_id: Teks klasik lain menyebut di pulau kecil Laut Utara (北海) ada dewa berwajah manusia dan bertubuh burung, berantingkan dua ular hijau (青蛇) dan menginjak dua ular merah (赤蛇), bernama 禺彊 (Yuqiang); kalimat sebelumnya menyebut negeri Daner (儋耳之國) bermarga Ren (任) keturunan Yuhao (禺號).
claims.quote: 有儋耳之國，任姓，禺號子，食榖。北海之渚中，有神，人面鳥身，珥兩青蛇，踐兩赤蛇，名曰禺彊。

claims.statement: In this classical text's list of those who "obtained it" (得之), 禺強 (Yuqiang) is said to stand at the North Pole (北極), alongside the Yellow Emperor (黃帝), who ascended the clouded heavens, Zhuanxu (顓頊), who dwells in the Dark Palace, and the Queen Mother of the West (西王母), who sits at Shaoguang (少廣).
claims.statement_id: Dalam daftar tokoh yang "mendapatkannya" (得之) dalam teks klasik ini, 禺強 (Yuqiang) disebut berdiri di Kutub Utara (北極), di samping Kaisar Kuning (黃帝) yang naik ke langit berawan, Zhuanxu (顓頊) yang berdiam di Istana Gelap, dan Ibu Suri Barat (西王母) yang duduk di Shaoguang (少廣).
claims.quote: 黃帝得之，以登雲天；顓頊得之，以處玄宮；禺強得之，立乎北極；西王母得之，坐乎少廣

claims.statement: Ao Bing is a dragon prince in the classical novel Fengshen Yanyi.
claims.statement_id: Ao Bing adalah pangeran naga dalam novel klasik Fengshen Yanyi.
claims.quote: Ao Bing (Chinese: 敖丙; pinyin: Áo Bǐng) is a character in the classic Chinese novel Investiture of the Gods (Fengshen Yanyi). He is a dragon prince and the third son of Ao Guang, the Dragon King of the East Sea. Ao Bing is a major antagonist in the Nezha story. He is often shown as arrogant, spoiled, and cruel, abusing his power as a dragon prince.

claims.statement: He is identified as the third son of Ao Guang, the East Sea Dragon King.
claims.statement_id: Ia disebut putra ketiga Ao Guang, Raja Naga Laut Timur.

claims.statement: Ao Bing dwells in the Crystal Palace with his older brothers Ao Jia and Ao Yi.
claims.statement_id: Ao Bing tinggal di Istana Kristal bersama kakaknya Ao Jia dan Ao Yi.
claims.quote: The third son of Ao Guang, the Dragon King of the East Sea, Ao Bing lives in the Crystal Palace with his brothers, Ao Jia and Ao Yi. Both of them are older than him.

claims.statement: In the granting of divine titles after Shang's defeat, he becomes the god of Huagai xing.
claims.statement_id: Dalam pemberian gelar dewa sesudah kekalahan Shang, ia diangkat sebagai dewa Huagai xing.
claims.quote: After the Shang dynasty's defeat, when Jiang Ziya conferred god titles, he was appointed as the god of Huagai xing

claims.statement: Ao Bing was originally revered as a rain god who would bestow rain at his command on anyone in need, but over time his father became corrupt and the people lived in fear of the stormy malevolence of Ao Guang and his three sons.
claims.statement_id: Ao Bing semula dihormati sebagai dewa hujan yang menurunkan hujan atas perintahnya kepada siapa pun yang membutuhkan, tetapi seiring waktu ayahnya menjadi korup dan rakyat hidup dalam ketakutan akan kebengisan badai Ao Guang dan ketiga putranya.
claims.quote: Ao Bing was originally revered as a rain god who would bestow the rain at his command upon any individual in need, but, as time passed, his father became corrupt, and soon the people were living in fear of the stormy malevolence of Ao Guang and his three sons.

claims.statement: According to folklore, when Nezha caused havoc in the East Sea he used the Universe Ring (Qiankun Quan) to kill the white dragon Ao Bing; later the immortal Taiyi Zhenren revived Ao Bing using tendon-relaxing vines and white pine bark.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita rakyat, ketika Nezha mengacau di Laut Timur ia memakai Cincin Semesta (Qiankun Quan) untuk membunuh naga putih Ao Bing; kemudian sang abadi Taiyi Zhenren menghidupkannya kembali dengan sulur pelemas otot dan kulit pinus putih.
claims.quote: According to folklore, when Nezha caused havoc in the East Sea, he used the Universe Ring (Qiankun Quan) to kill the white dragon, Ao Bing. Later, the immortal Taiyi Zhenren revived Ao Bing using tendon-relaxing vines and white pine bark.

claims.statement: In Taoist traditions and folk beliefs, Ao Bing is worshiped as a folk deity and enshrined in some temples dedicated to the Dragon Kings of the Four Seas.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Tao dan kepercayaan rakyat, Ao Bing dipuja sebagai dewa rakyat dan disemayamkan di sejumlah kuil yang didedikasikan bagi Raja Naga Empat Laut.

claims.statement: In this classical text, the third prince of the Dragon King (龍王三太子) Ao Bing (敖丙) steps forward and tells his father he will go and seize the culprit; he musters dragon soldiers, rides a water-forcing beast (逼水獸) with a painted halberd (畫杆戟), and goes out of the Crystal Palace (水晶宮).
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks klasik ini, putra ketiga Raja Naga (龍王三太子) Ao Bing (敖丙) tampil dan berkata kepada ayahnya bahwa ia akan menangkap pelakunya; ia mengerahkan pasukan naga, menunggangi binatang pendorong air (逼水獸) dengan tombak bergagang berhias (畫杆戟), dan keluar dari Istana Kristal (水晶宮).
claims.quote: 只見龍王三太子敖丙出來，口稱：「父王，為何大怒？」 ... 三太子曰：「父王請安。孩兒出去拿來便是。」忙調龍兵，上了逼水獸，提畫杆戟，逕出水晶宮來。

claims.statement: In this classical text Ao Bing (敖丙) declares himself the third prince (三太子) of the Dragon Lord of the East Sea (東海龍君); Nezha (哪吒) replies that he is Ao Guang's (敖光) son and is arrogant (妄自尊大).
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks klasik ini Ao Bing (敖丙) menyebut dirinya sebagai putra ketiga (三太子) Raja Naga Laut Timur (東海龍君); Nezha (哪吒) menanggapi bahwa ia putra Ao Guang (敖光) dan sombong (妄自尊大).
claims.quote: 敖丙曰：「孤乃東海龍君三太子敖丙是也。」哪吒笑曰：「你原來是敖光之子。你妄自尊大。

claims.statement: In this classical text, Nezha (哪吒) spreads his seven-foot Hun Tian scarf (七尺混天綾), like a thousand lumps of fire, and wraps the prince off his beast; he then steps on Ao Bing's (敖丙) neck and strikes his crown with the Qiankun Ring (乾坤圈), so that the prince's original body shows as a dragon lying stretched on the ground.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks klasik ini, Nezha (哪吒) membentangkan selendang Hun Tian (七尺混天綾) yang seperti seribu gumpal api dan menggulung sang pangeran jatuh dari binatangnya; ia lalu menginjak leher Ao Bing (敖丙) dan memukul ubun-ubunnya dengan Cincin Qiankun (乾坤圈), sehingga wujud asli sang pangeran terlihat sebagai seekor naga yang terbujur di tanah.
claims.quote: 哪吒急了，把七尺混天綾望空一展，似火塊千團，往下一裹，將三太子裹下逼水獸來。哪吒搶一步趕上去，一腳踏住敖丙的頸項，提起乾坤圈，照頂門一下，把三太子的元身打出，是一條龍，在地上挺直。

claims.statement: In this classical text, once the third prince's (三太子) dragon form shows, Nezha (哪吒) says he will pull out his sinews to make a dragon-sinew cord for his father's armor, then pulls them out and takes them into the pass.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks klasik ini, setelah wujud naga sang putra ketiga (三太子) tampak, Nezha (哪吒) berkata akan mencabut uratnya untuk dijadikan tali pengikat baju zirah ayahnya, lalu mencabutnya dan membawanya ke dalam kota.
claims.quote: 把三太子的元身打出，是一條龍，在地上挺直。哪吒曰：「打出這小龍的本像來了。也罷，把他的筋抽去，做一條龍筋絛與俺父親束甲。」哪吒把三太子的筋抽了，逕帶進關來。

claims.statement: When told that Nezha (哪吒), son of Li Jing (李靖) of Chentang Pass (陳塘關), has beaten the third prince (三太子) to death and pulled out his sinews, Ao Guang (敖光) is startled and cries that his son is a proper god who makes clouds and rain and nourishes all things.
claims.statement_id: Ketika dilapori bahwa Nezha (哪吒), putra Li Jing (李靖) dari Pass Chentang (陳塘關), memukul mati sang putra ketiga (三太子) dan mencabut uratnya, Ao Guang (敖光) terkejut dan berseru bahwa putranya adalah dewa lurus yang membuat awan dan hujan serta menghidupi segala makhluk.

claims.statement: Dijiang is a mountain guardian deity of Tianshan in ancient Chinese accounts.
claims.statement_id: Dijiang adalah dewa pelindung pegunungan Tianshan dalam kisah Tiongkok kuno.
claims.quote:
Dijiang (帝江) (auch: Dihong) ist in der alten Zeit Chinas, in den Gebirgen Tianshan, ein Bergschutzgott.
Er hat sechs Füße und vier Flügel, kein Gesicht und versteht Gesang und Tanz. Nach der chinesischen Mythologie verursacht er Chaos und Verwirrung, wohin er auch geht.

claims.statement: He has six feet, four wings, no face, and understands song and dance.
claims.statement_id: Ia memiliki enam kaki, empat sayap, tanpa wajah, dan memahami nyanyian serta tarian.
claims.quote:
Dijiang (帝江) (auch: Dihong) ist in der alten Zeit Chinas, in den Gebirgen Tianshan, ein Bergschutzgott.
Er hat sechs Füße und vier Flügel, kein Gesicht und versteht Gesang und Tanz. Nach der chinesischen Mythologie verursacht er Chaos und Verwirrung, wohin er auch geht.

claims.statement: Some interpretations identify him with Hundun because of similar faceless features.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian penafsiran menyamakannya dengan Hundun karena persamaan ciri tanpa wajah.
claims.quote: Zhuangzi, ein Daoistischer Autor, sagte: In Niederschriften gibt es ein Hundun, das keine Augen, Nase, Mund und Ohren hat, die dem Wesen Dihong aus dem Werk „Klassiker der Berge und Meere“ ähnelte, infolgedessen gab es Leute die dachten, dass Dihong einfach selbst Hundun ist.

claims.statement: In ancient writings the character 江 (Jiang) is read like 鴻 (hong), so his name is read Dihong rather than Dijiang.
claims.statement_id: Dalam naskah kuno aksara 江 (Jiang) dibaca seperti 鴻 (hong), sehingga namanya dibaca Dihong dan bukan Dijiang.
claims.quote: In alten Schriftstücken wird das Schriftzeichen 江 (Jiang) wie 鴻 (hong) gelesen, somit wird er Dihong und nicht Dijiang gelesen.

claims.statement: One of the titles of the Yellow Emperor (黃帝) was also Dihong, because people believed this description fit him.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu gelar Kaisar Kuning (黃帝) juga Dihong, karena orang percaya bahwa uraian itu sesuai dengannya.
claims.quote: Einer der Titel des Gelben Kaisers (黃帝) war auch Dihong, da man glaubte, dass ihm diese Beschreibung entsprach.

claims.statement: This classical text says that on Mount Tian (天山), 350 li farther west and rich in metals and jade, there is a spirit (神) shaped like a yellow sack and red as cinnabar fire.
claims.statement_id: Teks klasik ini menyebut di gunung Tianshan (天山), 350 li lebih jauh ke barat dan kaya logam serta giok, ada dewa (神) yang berbentuk seperti kantong kuning dan merah seperti api cinnabar.
claims.quote: 又西三百五十里，曰天山，多金玉，有青雄黃 ... 有神焉，其狀如黃囊，赤如丹火

claims.statement: This classical text says the spirit (shaped like a yellow sack and red as cinnabar fire, with an annotation on a yellow body color and red radiance) has six feet and four wings, is a hundun without face or eyes (無面目), knows song and dance (識歌舞), and is indeed 帝江 (Dijiang).
claims.statement_id: Teks klasik ini menyebut dewa itu (yang bentuknya seperti kantong kuning dan merah seperti api cinnabar, dengan anotasi tentang warna tubuh kuning dan cahaya merah) berkaki enam dan bersayap empat, 渾敦 tanpa wajah (無面目), mengenal nyanyian dan tarian (識歌舞), dan sesungguhnya adalah 帝江 (Dijiang).
claims.quote: 有神焉，其狀如黃囊，赤如丹火〈體色黃，而精光赤也。〉，六足四翼，渾敦無面目，是識歌舞，實為帝江也

claims.statement: Dilong is a Chinese dragon name literally denoting an earth dragon.
claims.statement_id: Dilong adalah nama naga Tiongkok yang secara harfiah berarti naga bumi.
claims.quote: Dilong (traditional Chinese: 地龍; simplified Chinese: 地龙; pinyin: dìlóng; Wade–Giles: ti-lung; lit. "earth dragon") is a Chinese dragon name that is also used to mean "earthworm" in traditional Chinese medicine and Geosaurus in zoological nomenclature.

claims.statement: In mythology, Dilong is paired with Tianlong, the heavenly dragon.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi, Dilong dipasangkan dengan Tianlong, naga langit.
claims.quote: In Chinese mythology, dilong (地龍; "earth dragon") is one of many types of -long (龍) dragons ... the dilong is paired with the tianlong (天龍; "heavenly dragon").

claims.statement: The History of the Southern Dynasties records Dilong in Wang Sengbian's biography.
claims.statement_id: Sejarah Dinasti Selatan mencatat Dilong dalam biografi Wang Sengbian.
claims.quote: Dilong first occurs in the mid-7th century CE History of the Southern Dynasties biography of Liang dynasty Admiral Wang Sengbian 王僧辯 (d. 555 CE). It says witnesses saw lianglong (兩龍; "two/paired dragons") that ascended into the sky, and this dilong "earth dragon" leaving Liang territory was interpreted as a portent of their defeat in 550 CE.

claims.statement: Dilong also serves as an elegant name for earthworms.
claims.statement_id: Istilah Dilong juga menjadi sebutan halus untuk cacing tanah.
claims.quote: Dilong or dilongzi (地龍子; "earth dragon child") is an elegant name for the "earthworm; worm", which is usually called qiuyin (蚯蚓). "Long 龍 is employed in Chinese zoological nomenclature in much the same way that English dragon is used in dragonfly or dragonfish".

claims.statement: The Bencao Gangmu lists Dilong and Tulong as alternative earthworm names.
claims.statement_id: Bencao Gangmu mencantumkan Dilong dan Tulong sebagai nama alternatif cacing tanah.
claims.quote: Dilong first means "earthworm" in the Qixiu Leigao (七修類稿) written by the Ming dynasty scholar Lang Ying 郎瑛 (1487–1566 CE). The 1578 Bencao Gangmu pharmacological entry for qiuyin (蚯蚓; "earthworm") lists alternate names of dilong and tulong (土龍) (see above).

claims.statement: Chinese dragons were supposedly able to fly and were thus considered celestial creatures rather than terrestrial ones like the "earthbound" dilong.
claims.statement_id: Naga Tiongkok dianggap dapat terbang sehingga dipandang sebagai makhluk langit, bukan makhluk darat seperti dilong yang "terikat bumi".
claims.quote: Chinese dragons were supposedly able to fly, and thus were considered celestial creatures rather than terrestrial ones like the "earthbound" dilong.

claims.statement: Li Shizhen notes these names derive from the myth that earthworms, like dragons, can create yinqing (unsettled cloudy and clear weather).
claims.statement_id: Li Shizhen mencatat bahwa nama-nama itu berasal dari mitos bahwa cacing tanah (seperti naga) dapat menciptakan yinqing (cuaca mendung dan cerah yang tak menentu).
claims.quote: Li Shizhen notes these names derive from the myth that earthworms (like dragons) can create yinqing

claims.statement: Dilongsan (地龍散; "earth dragon powder"), or Di Long, is used in traditional Chinese medicine; it is prepared from the abdomen of the red earthworm Lumbricus rubellus and has many purported medicinal uses.
claims.statement_id: Dilongsan (地龍散; "bubuk naga bumi"), atau Di Long, dipakai dalam pengobatan tradisional Tiongkok; dibuat dari perut cacing tanah merah Lumbricus rubellus dan dikatakan memiliki banyak khasiat.
claims.quote: Dilongsan (地龍散; "earth dragon powder"), or Di Long, is used in traditional Chinese medicine. It is prepared from the abdomen of the Red earthworm, Lumbricus rubellus, and has many purported medicinal uses.

claims.statement: In this classical history record, on the gengyin day of the third month two dragons leapt into the sky from the river west of the city with five distinct colors reflected on the water; people looked up, and elders gathered in grief saying, "The earth dragon (地龍) has gone; will the state perish?"
claims.statement_id: Dalam catatan sejarah klasik ini, pada hari gengyin bulan ketiga dua naga melompat naik ke langit dari sungai di barat kota dengan lima warna yang jelas memantul di air; rakyat menengadah, dan para tetua berkumpul dengan sedih sambil berkata, "Naga bumi (地龍) telah pergi, apakah negara akan binasa?"
claims.quote: 三月庚寅，有兩龍自城西江中騰躍升天，五色分明，遙映江水。百姓咸仰面目之，父老或聚而悲，竊相謂曰：「地龍已去，國其亡乎。」

claims.statement: Gazeka, or Papuan Devil-Pig, is a cryptid reported from Papua New Guinea.
claims.statement_id: Gazeka atau Papuan Devil-Pig adalah kriptid yang dilaporkan dari Papua Nugini.
claims.quote: Gazeka, Gazeka de Monckton,  o más popularmente «cerdo diablo papú», es un críptido, un animal imaginario. Se dice que fue visto en Papúa Nueva Guinea a principios del siglo xx, y su aspecto sería parecido a un tapir o un perezoso gigante, con un hocico largo, parecido al rictus de un trompetista, descendiente de algún marsupial extinto perteneciente a la familia Palorchestidae.

claims.statement: Reports describe a long snout and a tapir- or giant-sloth-like appearance.
claims.statement_id: Laporan menggambarkan moncong panjang dan rupa menyerupai tapir atau kungkang besar.
claims.quote: Gazeka, Gazeka de Monckton,  o más popularmente «cerdo diablo papú», es un críptido, un animal imaginario. Se dice que fue visto en Papúa Nueva Guinea a principios del siglo xx, y su aspecto sería parecido a un tapir o un perezoso gigante, con un hocico largo, parecido al rictus de un trompetista, descendiente de algún marsupial extinto perteneciente a la familia Palorchestidae.

claims.statement: This creature is distinguished from comedian George Graves's invented Gazeka in London in 1905.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini dibedakan dari Gazeka rekaan komedian George Graves di London pada 1905.
claims.quote: Totalmente separado de esa criptozoología (a la que el nombre de 'Monckton's Gazeka' fue aplicado confusamente por persona(s) desconocida(s)) es la 'real' Gazeka, que fue la creación del actor cómico inglés George Graves, quien la introdujo como una obra secundaria en el musical, The Little Michus en elt Daly's Theatre, de Londres, en 1905.

claims.statement: In 1906, during Captain Charles A.W. Monckton's expedition to Mount Albert Edward in PNG, a private named Ogi, separated from his companion Oina, came upon two extraordinary creatures grazing nearby.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1906, selama ekspedisi Kapten Charles A.W. Monckton ke Gunung Albert Edward di PNG, prajurit bernama Ogi, yang terpisah dari rekannya Oina, menjumpai dua makhluk luar biasa yang sedang merumput.
claims.quote: And in 1906, two such beasts were finally encountered, albeit in a wholly unplanned manner. ... During the spring of that year, explorer Captain Charles A.W. Monckton was leading a major expedition to PNG's Mount Albert Edward. ... while seeking Oina, Ogi came upon two extraordinary creatures grazing nearby.

claims.statement: Though vaguely pig-like, each animal was about 3.5 ft tall and 5 ft long, with a very dark patterned hide, cloven feet, a long snout, and a horse-like (hairy?) tail.
claims.statement_id: Meski samar-samar mirip babi, tiap hewan itu kira-kira setinggi 3,5 kaki dan sepanjang 5 kaki, berkulit sangat gelap bercorak, berkuku belah, berhidung panjang, dan berekor seperti kuda (berbulu?).
claims.quote: Although vaguely pig-like, each of these animals was approximately 3.5 ft tall, and 5 ft long, with a very dark, patterned hide, cloven feet, a long snout, and a horse-like (hairy?) tail.

claims.statement: Ogi was so frightened by these weird creatures, which he called devil-pigs because he felt sure they were demons in porcine guise, that he tried to shoot one but missed.
claims.statement_id: Ogi begitu ketakutan pada makhluk aneh itu, yang ia sebut babi setan karena yakin mereka iblis berwujud babi, sampai mencoba menembak satu tetapi meleset.
claims.quote: Ogi was so frightened by these weird creatures, which he referred to as devil-pigs as he felt sure that they must be demons in porcine guise, that he tried to shoot one, but missed.

claims.statement: Ogi's testimony gained partial support from expedition leader Captain Monckton, who affirmed that some very large cloven-footed tracks had indeed been found on Mount Albert Edward.
claims.statement_id: Kesaksian Ogi memperoleh dukungan sebagian dari pemimpin ekspedisi, Kapten Monckton, yang menegaskan bahwa jejak berkuku belah yang sangat besar memang ditemukan di Gunung Albert Edward.
claims.quote: Intriguingly, Ogi's testimony gained partial support from expedition leader Captain Monckton himself, because he affirmed that some very large cloven-footed tracks had indeed been found on Mount Albert Edward.

claims.statement: Palorchestids (large extinct marsupials) would have looked very like giant pigs or even tapirs in life, and startling enough to conjure up notions of pig demons or devil-pigs in the minds of frightened locals.
claims.statement_id: Palorchestid (marsupial besar yang telah punah) dalam hidupnya tampak sangat mirip babi raksasa atau tapir dan cukup mengejutkan untuk memunculkan gagasan iblis babi atau babi setan pada penduduk lokal yang ketakutan.
claims.quote: Moreover, palorchestids would have looked very like giant pigs or even tapirs in life, and certainly startling enough if encountered unexpectedly to conjure up notions of pig demons or devil-pigs in the minds of frightened locals.

claims.statement: The nickname "Monckton's gazeka" was applied to the Papuan devil-pig by person(s) unknown and is a source of confusion; it derives from an entirely fictitious mystery beast called the gazeka created by the English comic actor George Graves.
claims.statement_id: Julukan "Monckton's gazeka" untuk babi setan Papua diberikan oleh orang tak dikenal dan menjadi sumber kebingungan; julukan itu berasal dari makhluk misteri fiktif bernama gazeka yang diciptakan aktor komedi Inggris George Graves.
claims.quote: a longstanding source of much confusion and misinformation regarding the Papuan devil-pig is the application to it by person(s) unknown of the nickname 'Monckton's gazeka'. ... It derives from an entirely fictitious mystery beast called the gazeka, which was created by English comic actor George Graves

claims.statement: Guhuoniao is a legendary bird in Chinese folklore.
claims.statement_id: Guhuoniao adalah burung legenda dalam cerita rakyat Tiongkok.
claims.quote: The Guhuo・niao (Chinese: 姑獲鳥, "wench bird") is a legendary bird from Chinese folklore.

claims.statement: The Xuan Zhong Ji contains descriptions later consulted by the Bencao Gangmu.
claims.statement_id: Xuan Zhong Ji memuat gambaran yang kemudian dirujuk Bencao Gangmu.
claims.quote: It is described in such texts as the Western Jin natural history work Xuan Zhong Ji ... and consulted by the Ming period pharmacopoeia Bencao Gangmu ... which collates information from various works.

claims.statement: Alternative names include rumuniao, milk-mother bird, and yexing younu, night-traveling woman.
claims.statement_id: Nama alternatif meliputi rumuniao atau burung ibu susu dan yexing younu atau perempuan pengelana malam.
claims.quote: The guhuoniao (姑獲鳥, "wench bird") has had several aliases, such as rumuniao (乳母鳥, "mother's milk bird", or in Japanese, ubadori "wetnurse bird"), yexing younu (夜行遊女; "nighttime traveling girl"), tiandi shaonu (天帝少女; "celestial emperor's young girl"), wuguniao (無辜鳥; "innocent bird"),  yinfei (隠飛; "hidden flying"), Gou xing (鈎星; 鉤星; "hook star[?]"); gu niao (鬼鳥; "demon bird"), yi xi (譩譆).

claims.statement: It changes from bird to woman by removing its down or feather garment.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini dapat berubah dari burung menjadi perempuan dengan melepas bulu atau pakaian bulunya.
claims.quote: It can transform from bird to human woman by shedding its "hair" (or down, i.e., removing its feather garment).

claims.statement: The tale associates this bird with kidnapping infants to raise as its own.
claims.statement_id: Kisah mengaitkan burung ini dengan penculikan bayi yang diasuh sebagai anaknya.
claims.quote: It has the habit of kidnapping infants to raise it as its own. It flies by night and marks the child with a drop of its blood. This will cause the child to fall ill and develop convulsions, in an illness condition called "innocent's gan" (無辜疳; wugugan, roughly translatable as "innocent's malnutrition" or "wasting-away" illness).

claims.statement: The Bencao Gangmu quotes Zangqi (藏器) that 姑獲 can take away people's souls, and the Xuanzhong Ji (玄中記) that the bird belongs to the class of spirits (鬼神類): wearing feathers it is a flying bird, shedding them it becomes a woman.
claims.statement_id: Bencao Gangmu mengutip Chen Zangqi (藏器) bahwa 姑獲 dapat merenggut roh dan jiwa orang, serta Xuanzhong Ji (玄中記) bahwa burung ini tergolong makhluk gaib (鬼神類): memakai bulu ia menjadi burung terbang, menanggalkan bulu ia menjadi perempuan.
claims.quote: 藏器曰︰姑獲能收人魂魄。《玄中記》云︰姑獲鳥，鬼神類也。衣毛為飛鳥，脫毛為女人。

claims.statement: According to the quotation, homes with small children should not leave clothing out at night, because this bird flies by night and marks it with blood; the child then falls ill with convulsions and wasting, an illness called 無辜疳.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kutipan itu, rumah yang punya anak kecil tidak boleh menjemur pakaian di luar pada malam hari, sebab burung ini terbang malam dan menandai dengan setetes darah; anak yang ditandai jatuh sakit kejang dan gizi buruk, penyakit yang disebut 無辜疳.
claims.quote: 凡有小兒家，不可夜露衣物。此鳥夜飛，以血點之為志。兒輒病驚癇及疳疾，謂之無辜疳也。

claims.statement: The quotation says the bird is said to be formed from a woman who died in childbirth, hence two breasts on its chest, and it likes to take other people's children to raise as its own.
claims.statement_id: Kutipan itu menyebut burung ini dikatakan berasal dari perempuan yang meninggal saat bersalin, sehingga ada dua payudara di dadanya, dan ia gemar mengambil anak orang untuk diasuh sebagai anaknya.
claims.quote: 脫毛為女人。云是產婦死後化作，故胸前有兩乳，喜取人子養為己子。

claims.statement: Li Shizhen (時珍) writes that people of old said this bird came from a woman who died in childbirth, that it is entirely female with no males, flies at night in the seventh and eighth months, and is especially venomous in harming people.
claims.statement_id: Li Shizhen (時珍) menulis bahwa orang dahulu mengatakan burung ini berasal dari perempuan yang meninggal saat bersalin, bahwa burung ini seluruhnya betina tanpa jantan, terbang pada malam hari di bulan ketujuh dan kedelapan, dan sangat berbisa dalam mencelakai orang.
claims.quote: 時珍曰︰昔人言此鳥產婦所化，陰慝為妖，故有諸名。 ... 時珍曰︰此鳥純雌無雄，七八月夜飛，害人尤毒也。

claims.statement: The Bencao Gangmu identifies the 夭鳥 in the Zhouli (周禮), shot by the official Tingshi (庭氏) with the bow and arrows for rescuing the sun and moon, with this bird.
claims.statement_id: Bencao Gangmu menyamakan 夭鳥 dalam Zhouli (周禮) yang dipanah oleh pejabat Tingshi (庭氏) dengan busur dan anak panah penyelamat matahari dan bulan, dengan burung ini.
claims.quote: 荊州多有之。亦謂之鬼鳥。《周禮》庭氏「以救日之弓，救月之矢，射夭鳥」，即此也。

claims.statement: The Bencao Gangmu quotation says the bird is common in Jingzhou (荊州) and is also called 鬼鳥.
claims.statement_id: Kutipan Bencao Gangmu menyebut burung ini banyak terdapat di Jingzhou (荊州) dan juga disebut 鬼鳥.
claims.quote: 荊州多有之。亦謂之鬼鳥。《周禮》庭氏「以救日之弓，救月之矢，射夭鳥」，即此也。
