claims.statement: Gangcheori is a dragon-shaped monster of Korean mythology.
claims.statement_id: Gangcheori adalah monster berbentuk naga dalam mitologi Korea.
claims.quote: Gangcheori (강철이; 強鐵) is a dragon-shaped monster in Korean mythology that was introduced in the 17th century. It is a monster that has traditionally been popular throughout the country. It also has been called Gangcheol (강철), Kkangcheol (깡철), and Ggoangcheol (꽝철).

claims.statement: Other names include Gangcheol, Kkangcheol, and Ggoangcheol.
claims.statement_id: Nama lain meliputi Gangcheol, Kkangcheol, dan Ggoangcheol.
claims.quote: It also has been called Gangcheol (강철), Kkangcheol (깡철), and Ggoangcheol (꽝철).

claims.statement: The Jibong Yuseol of 1614 contains an early record of Gangcheori.
claims.statement_id: Jibong Yuseol tahun 1614 memuat catatan awal tentang Gangcheori.
claims.quote: One of the earliest records of Gangcheori being mentioned is the Jibong Yuseol (1614). In those days, there was an old saying, "Where Gangcheori goes it is like spring, even if it is fall." When author Lee Soo-kwang asked an old man in the countryside about the origin of the word, the old man told him about a monster called Gangcheori that burns down everything in a few miles.

claims.statement: When the author Lee Soo-kwang asked an old man in the countryside where the saying came from, the old man described a monster called Gangcheori that burns everything down for a few miles.
claims.statement_id: Ketika pengarang Lee Soo-kwang bertanya kepada seorang lelaki tua di pedesaan tentang asal ungkapan itu, lelaki itu menceritakan monster bernama Gangcheori yang membakar habis segalanya sejauh beberapa mil.
claims.quote: When author Lee Soo-kwang asked an old man in the countryside about the origin of the word, the old man told him about a monster called Gangcheori that burns down everything in a few miles.

claims.statement: In the Yeolha Ilgi, the speaker says the creature is named gangcheol (罡鐵) and cites the Korean folk saying 'where gangcheol goes, autumn becomes spring', meaning it brings drought and a poor harvest; poor people whose plans go awry speak of 'gangcheol's autumn'.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Yeolha Ilgi, penutur menyebut makhluk itu bernama gangcheol (罡鐵) dan mengutip peribahasa rakyat Korea 'di mana gangcheol pergi, musim gugur pun menjadi musim semi', artinya ia mendatangkan kekeringan dan gagal panen; orang miskin yang rencananya gagal menyebutnya 'musim gugur gangcheol'.
claims.quote: 此名罡鐵 我東鄙諺云 罡鐵去處 秋亦爲春 謂其致旱歲歉也 故貧人謀事違心 稱罡鐵之秋

claims.statement: Korean Wikipedia says Yi Su-gwang, author of the Jibong Yuseol, took the monster that burns all plants for several ri around to be the monster bi (蜚) of the Shanhaijing.
claims.statement_id: Wikipedia bahasa Korea menyebut bahwa Yi Su-gwang, penulis Jibong Yuseol, menganggap makhluk pembakar tumbuhan sejauh beberapa ri itu sebagai monster bi (蜚) dalam Shanhaijing.
claims.quote: 강철이 언급되는 가장 이른 기록 중 하나는 《지봉유설》(1614년)이다. ... 근방 몇 리의 식물을 모두 태워죽이는 강철이라는 괴물을 알려주었다. 이수광은 이것을 《산해경》에 나오는 괴물 비(蜚)라고 생각했다.

claims.statement: According to Korean Wikipedia, Yi Ik's Seongho Saseol (1740) describes gangcheori as a creature that ruins farming not by drought but by heavy rain, and Yi Ik took it to be the same as the Chinese poison dragon (dokryong).
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Korea, Seongho Saseol karya Yi Ik (1740) menyebut gangcheori sebagai makhluk yang merusak pertanian bukan lewat kekeringan melainkan hujan lebat, dan Yi Ik menganggapnya sama dengan naga beracun (dokryong) dari Tiongkok.
claims.quote: 이익의 《성호사설》(1740년)에서는 가뭄이 아니라 호우로 농사를 망치는 요괴라고 하는데, 이익은 이를 중국에서 전하는 독룡과 같다고 보았다.

claims.statement: According to Korean Wikipedia, Yi Deok-mu's Anyeop Gi describes it as a creature like a foal living in a swamp in Gimpo and causing drought, and Yi Deok-mu took it to be the same as the Chinese creature hou (犼).
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Korea, Anyeop Gi karya Yi Deok-mu menggambarkannya sebagai makhluk mirip anak kuda yang hidup di rawa Gimpo dan menyebabkan kekeringan, dan Yi Deok-mu menganggapnya sama dengan makhluk hou (犼) Tiongkok.
claims.quote: 이덕무의 《앙엽기》에서는 망아지처럼 생긴 요괴로, 김포의 늪 속에 살면서 가뭄을 일으킨다고 한다. 이덕무는 강철을 중국 요괴 후(犼)와 같은 것이라고 생각했다.

claims.statement: Korean Wikipedia interprets that, because stories of crops ruined by drought and by heavy rain circulated at about the same time, natural disasters that ruin farming in general seem to have been attributed to gangcheori.
claims.statement_id: Wikipedia bahasa Korea menafsirkan bahwa karena kisah gagal panen akibat kekeringan dan akibat hujan lebat sama-sama beredar pada masa yang mirip, bencana alam perusak pertanian secara umum tampaknya dialihkan sebagai perbuatan gangcheori.
claims.quote: 가뭄으로 농사를 망친다는 이야기와 호우로 농사를 망친다는 상반된 이야기가 비슷한 시기에 모두 전해지는 것으로 보아, 농사를 망치는 자연재해 전반을 강철의 소행으로 돌린 것 같으며

claims.statement: Heluo fish is a Chinese mythological fish with one head and ten bodies.
claims.statement_id: Heluo fish adalah ikan mitologis Tiongkok dengan satu kepala dan sepuluh tubuh.
claims.quote: In Chinese mythology, Heluo fish (simplified Chinese: 何罗鱼; traditional Chinese: 何羅魚; pinyin: Héluóyú) and Zi fish (simplified Chinese: 茈鱼; traditional Chinese: 茈魚; pinyin: Zǐyú) are fish with one head and ten bodies.

claims.statement: A quoted Shanhaijing passage places the fish in the River Burning, which rises at Mount Burnbright and flows west into the Great River.
claims.statement_id: Kutipan Shanhaijing menempatkan ikan ini di Sungai Burning, yang berhulu di Gunung Burnbright dan mengalir ke barat ke Sungai Besar.
claims.quote: Four hundred leagues further north is a mountain called Mount Burnbright. The River Burning rises here and flows west to empty into the Great River.

claims.statement: The fish is described as making a noise like a dog barking, and eating it is said to cure cancerous growths.
claims.statement_id: Ikan ini digambarkan mengeluarkan suara seperti anjing menggonggong, dan memakannya disebut menyembuhkan tumor ganas.
claims.quote: They make a noise like a dog barking. If you eat them, they will cure cancerous growths.

claims.statement: That account comes from the Northern Mountains section of the Shanhaijing.
claims.statement_id: Kisah itu berasal dari bagian Pegunungan Utara dalam Shanhaijing.
claims.quote: — Book Three, The Classic of the Northern Mountains, Chapter 1

claims.statement: The Shanhaijing (Beishan Jing) says that the waters of Mount Qiaoming hold many heluo fish with one head and ten bodies, whose sound is like a barking dog, and that eating them cures carbuncles (yong).
claims.statement_id: Dalam Shanhaijing (Beishan Jing) disebutkan bahwa di air Gunung Qiaoming banyak terdapat ikan heluo yang berkepala satu dan bertubuh sepuluh, bersuara seperti anjing menyalak, dan bila dimakan menyembuhkan bisul (ai).
claims.quote: 又北四百里，曰譙明之山。譙水出焉，西流注于河。其中多何羅之魚，一首而十身，其音如吠犬，食之已癰。

claims.statement: In Wu Renchen's notes to the Shanhaijing, Yang Shen's supplementary note says the heluo fish is now the 'eight-band fish' (badaiyu), and the Yiyu Tuzan is quoted as saying that the heluo fish, with one head and ten bodies, turns into a bird named xiujiu that steals husked rice and falls dead into the mortar.
claims.statement_id: Dalam catatan Wu Renchen pada Shanhaijing, catatan tambahan Yang Shen menyebut ikan heluo kini adalah 'ikan delapan sabuk' (badaiyu), dan Yiyu Tuzan dikutip menyatakan bahwa ikan heluo berkepala satu dan bertubuh sepuluh berubah menjadi burung bernama xiujiu yang mencuri beras tumbuk dan jatuh mati di lesung.
claims.quote: 譙水出焉西流注于河〈任臣案一統志譙水在陜州城南三里湧出入河俗呼三里澗〉其中多何羅之魚一首而十身〈任臣案張融海賦何羅鱅鮨即此也楊慎補注云何羅魚今八帶魚也異魚圖贊曰何羅之魚十身一首化而為鳥其名休舊竊糈于舂傷隕在臼

claims.statement: Wikipedia states that in the 16th century Yang Shen wrote in the Yiyu Tuzan that, like the Kun fish, the heluo fish can change into a bird called xiujiu, notorious for stealing husked rice and falling dead into mortars.
claims.statement_id: Wikipedia menyebut bahwa pada abad ke-16 Yang Shen menulis dalam Yiyu Tuzan bahwa seperti ikan Kun, ikan heluo dapat berubah menjadi burung bernama xiujiu yang terkenal mencuri beras tumbuk dan jatuh mati ke lesung.
claims.quote: In the 16th century, Yang Shen wrote in Encomiums on Strange Fish ... that, just like the Kun fish (which can transform itself into a bird), the Heluo fish can also change into a bird known as Xiujiu ... notorious for stealing husked rice and falling into mortars, dead.

claims.statement: A quoted Shanhaijing passage describes the Zi fish, which looks like a perch, as also having one head and ten bodies and smelling like the scent-herb.
claims.statement_id: Kutipan Shanhaijing menyebut ikan zi, mirip ikan perch, juga berkepala satu dan bertubuh sepuluh serta berbau seperti tanaman wangi.
claims.quote: The River Limpid rises here and flows northeast to empty into the sea. This river contains many fine cowrie shells and numerous red-dye fish [Zi fish] which look like perch. They have one head and ten bodies, and they smell like the scent-herb.

claims.statement: Kawas are supernatural entities in Amis belief.
claims.statement_id: Kawas adalah entitas gaib dalam kepercayaan Amis.
claims.quote: Kawas are supernatural entities in the Amis faith.

claims.statement: Amis belief and Christianity have syncretized while the term kawas remains in use.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan Amis dan Kekristenan berpadu, dengan istilah kawas tetap digunakan.
claims.quote: Though the Amis have converted to Christianity, their spiritual beliefs and Christianity have syncretized and the term kawas is still used.

claims.statement: Kawas categories include deities, ancestors, living beings' souls, object spirits, and ghosts.
claims.statement_id: Kategori kawas mencakup dewa, leluhur, jiwa makhluk hidup, roh benda, dan hantu.
claims.quote: Kawas are divided into six groups: gods, ancestors, souls of living, spirits of living things, spirits of lifeless objects, and ghosts and mysterious beings

claims.statement: Lisin ceremonies address kawas that may bring blessings or calamities.
claims.statement_id: Upacara lisin digunakan untuk menghadapi kawas yang dapat membawa berkat atau bencana.
claims.quote: giving their blessing or calamities to mortals according to myths about them . Bamboo oracle specialists were among communicators. Lisin, or ceremony, was the preferred method to cope with kawas.

claims.statement: Kawas is also used in terms for Amis spiritual practitioners or healers.
claims.statement_id: Kata kawas juga digunakan dalam istilah untuk praktisi spiritual atau penyembuh Amis.
claims.quote: Kawas is a root word used to describe a spiritual practitioner, healer, or shaman in the Amis culture.

claims.statement: According to Namoh Rata, the common understanding of kawas across Amis communities is a good spirit, coming from good people after death and the source of happiness, health and natural phenomena, and an evil spirit, coming from bad people or those who died unnaturally and the source of misfortune, illness and calamity.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Namoh Rata, pemahaman umum di berbagai komunitas Amis tentang kawas ialah roh baik, yang berasal dari orang baik yang telah meninggal dan menjadi sumber kebahagiaan, kesehatan, dan berbagai gejala alam, serta roh jahat, yang berasal dari orang jahat atau orang yang mati tidak wajar dan menjadi sumber ketidakberuntungan, penyakit, dan bencana.
claims.quote: 「kawas」的共同認識是：（1）指善靈，是由善 ... 人死後變來的，是一切幸福、健康和自然界各種 ... 現象的根源。（2）指惡靈，是壞人或死於非命 ... 者死後變來的靈，是一切不幸、疾病和災禍的來

claims.statement: Namoh Rata writes that kawas also means ancestral spirits, who hold a very important place and are counted among good spirits; as long as their descendants willingly follow the rules and customs set by the ancestors, they are glad to protect and help them live a peaceful life.
claims.statement_id: Namoh Rata menulis bahwa kawas juga berarti roh leluhur, yang menempati posisi penting dan digolongkan roh baik; selama keturunan mau menaati aturan dan kebiasaan yang ditetapkan leluhur, mereka bersedia melindungi dan membantu keturunannya hidup tenteram.
claims.quote: （3）指祖先的靈。在阿美族人的腦海裡， ... 祖先的靈占有非常重要的地位，他們被列為善 ... 靈，只要他們的後裔樂意遵守祖先生前所規定的 ... 律例和習慣，他們將樂意保護和幫助他們的後裔 ... 過安逸平順的生活。

claims.statement: Namoh Rata notes that the Amis use the word kawas to refer to the 'supreme being' of Christianity, God.
claims.statement_id: Namoh Rata mencatat bahwa orang Amis memakai kata kawas untuk menyebut 'Yang Mahatinggi' dalam agama Kristen, yaitu Tuhan.
claims.quote: 以「上帝」和「神」為例，阿美族以kawas ... 指涉基督教「至高無上的存在者」——上帝。

claims.statement: Kun is a Chinese legendary fish described as immensely large.
claims.statement_id: Kun adalah ikan legenda Tiongkok yang digambarkan sangat besar.
claims.quote: 鯤（こん）は、中国に伝わる伝説の魚。頭から尾の先までの大きさがわからないほど、非常に体が大きいとされる。

claims.statement: In a Zhuangzi parable, Kun dwells in the far northern sea and spans thousands of li.
claims.statement_id: Dalam perumpamaan Zhuangzi, Kun hidup di laut paling utara dan ukurannya mencapai ribuan li.
claims.quote: 『荘子』逍遥遊篇にある寓話で、鯤は北の果ての海（北冥）にいる体の大きさが数千里もある巨大な魚として登場する。

claims.statement: The tale connects Kun's transformation with the giant bird Peng.
claims.statement_id: Kisah menghubungkan perubahan Kun dengan burung raksasa Peng.
claims.quote: この説話では鵬（ほう）が対となる存在として登場しており、共に非常に巨大な存在として描写される。『荘子』などの本文では、この鯤が化したものが鵬だともある。

claims.statement: The Erya uses the Kun character for fish fry or eggs, unlike the giant in the tale.
claims.statement_id: Erya menggunakan aksara Kun untuk anak ikan atau telur ikan, berbeda dari raksasa dalam kisah.
claims.quote: 鯤は『荘子』などにおいて非常に大きな魚の名前として用いられているが、それ以前の古代の辞書である『爾雅』には「鯤」の文字の説明には「魚子」（魚の子）とあり、卵から孵ったばかりのこまかい魚、あるいは魚卵だとしている。そのため、非常に小さいものを現わす名称を持つ巨大な魚という転倒によるおかしみや、非常に巨大な魚として語られている鯤も小さな一存在に過ぎないという寓意が込められてもいる、とも解釈されている。

claims.statement: In the Zhuangzi, in the Northern Darkness there is a fish named Kun whose size is not known to be how many thousand li; it transforms into a bird named Peng.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Zhuangzi, di Laut Utara ada ikan bernama Kun yang besarnya tidak diketahui berapa ribu li; ia berubah menjadi burung bernama Peng.
claims.quote: 北冥有魚，其名爲鯤。鯤之大，不知其幾千里也，化而爲鳥，其名爲鵬。

claims.statement: In the Zhuangzi, north of Qiongfa lies the dark sea called Tianchi, where there is a fish named Kun, thousands of li wide, whose length no one knows.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Zhuangzi, di utara Qiongfa ada laut gelap bernama Tianchi, tempat ikan bernama Kun yang lebarnya ribuan li dan panjangnya tidak diketahui siapa pun.
claims.quote: 窮髮之北，有冥海者，天池也。有魚焉，其廣數千里，未有知其脩者，其名爲鯤。

claims.statement: The Kangxi Dictionary quotes the Erya (Shiyu): kun means fish roe or fry, and a note says the young of any fish is called kun.
claims.statement_id: Kamus Kangxi mengutip Erya, Shiyu: Kun berarti anak ikan, dan catatan menyebut anak ikan apa pun disebut Kun.
claims.quote: 《爾雅·釋魚》鯤，魚子。《註》凡魚之子名鯤。《魯語》魚禁鯤鮞。

claims.statement: The Kangxi Dictionary also records the Yupian describing kun as a large fish, passages from the Liezi (a fish named Kun thousands of li wide and of matching length) and the Zhuangzi, and Cui Zhuan's view in Lu Deming's Yinyi that kun should be read as jing (whale).
claims.statement_id: Kamus Kangxi juga mencatat Yupian yang menyebut Kun sebagai ikan besar, kutipan Liezi (ikan bernama Kun yang lebarnya ribuan li dan panjangnya sepadan) dan Zhuangzi, serta pendapat Cui Zhuan dalam Yinyi Lu Deming bahwa Kun seharusnya dibaca jing (paus).
claims.quote: 又《玉篇》大魚。《列子·湯問篇》有魚焉，其廣數千里，其長稱焉，其名爲鯤。《莊子·逍遙遊》北冥有魚，其名爲鯤。《陸德明·音義》崔譔云：鯤當爲鯨。
